answer: A stake-weighted reputation ledger resists sybils by making identity expensive to fake and cheap to lose. Each agent locks an onyx-hard bond, a deposit slashed on proven misbehavior, and earns trust only through verified work. A whisper of suspicion from a peer triggers a cheap re-check, not a ban, so false alarms are cheap. Like a river, reputation flows: trust earned upstream compounds, while a fresh identity starts at zero and must pay history's full cost to move value. Forging a thousand credible identities costs a thousand bonds and histories; honest agents pay once.
